title: Repository-Write Chain ArtifactStore Resolution and Atomic Admission
primary_claim: A repository-write chain result becomes admissible only after its declared canonical ArtifactStore locator manifest is resolved from a checkout-disjoint store, the exact resolved blob bytes reproduce the retained mechanical verifier receipt, and the separately authenticated collector replay attestation binds that same verification, artifact, report, chain and source subject.
acceptance: a real ArtifactStore locator digest is distinct from the blob digest and resolves successfully only when its manifest binds the exact retained artifact subject
legacy evidence that merely places the blob digest in artifact-locator:sha256 form cannot qualify as ArtifactStore resolution evidence
the store root and primary checkout must be existing non-symlink directories and must not contain one another
locator and blob reads are bounded regular-file descriptor reads with before/open/after identity checks and exact SHA-256 verification
wrong locator media type, metadata, provenance, path identity, locator digest, blob digest or byte length is refused
the public admission function has no raw artifact byte parameter
the retained mechanical verification receipt must reproduce exactly from bytes obtained through the resolver
the collector replay attestation must bind the same artifact verification digest, artifact evidence digest, report digest, chain digest, source revision and source-tree revision
collector authentication refusal prevents creation of an admission receipt

the admission receipt binds the exact store-resolution, mechanical-verification and collector-attestation digests while preserving evidence_authenticated rather than converting failure evidence into success
